01 — Far

25,900,000,000km

Voyager 1, right now. About one light-day from Earth.

In 1977, people sent a machine the size of a small car into space. It has been flying for 49 years. It still sends home 160 bits every second.

Big things are mostly small things, done carefully, for a long time. That is the part I try to get right.

This is home.

In 1990, Voyager 1 turned its camera around, six billion kilometres out, and took one last picture of us.

Everyone you have ever known lived on that dot.

Everything anyone has ever built was built there. Webb. Voyager. The chip in your hand.

It is worth making good things here.

You are here

After Voyager 1's "Pale Blue Dot", 14 February 1990. A drawing, not the photo.
